findings.summary: static module URLs and closed-directory discovery registered the same local file under relative and absolute identities, doubling LibreQuake's manifest and payload; local asset registration now canonicalizes existing files to one entry-relative portable source

dynamic candidate expansion retained duplicate logical keys when a directly named file was also found beneath a candidate directory; one keyed candidate table now removes the duplicate before emitting C++

staticAssetUrlCandidates walked every reached source file for each runtime-selected fetch encountered while lowering LibreQuake; the source graph is immutable during one compile, so the sorted result is cached once

finally-block emission captured lines without a compiler lexical scope, allowing declarations created inside the finalizer to leak into later lowering; capture now pushes and pops its own block scope while retaining the native scope guard
class recursion detection rebuilt the class method graph at every call site; its result is invariant per method and is now cached for the compiler lifetime

three shader system-uniform accessors independently searched the same metadata table and repeated the same missing-row guard; one total row lookup now serves enumerator, type, and packed-size projection

generation-time fetch detection stopped at the direct helper, so an otherwise native-eligible wrapper converted a static template URL into a runtime string before the nested fetch was specialized; the detector now follows the local call graph with cycle and result caches

the registry-wide parity runner launched every audio-enabled application beside the parallel GPU batch, allowing LabSound hardware contexts in separate processes to race during teardown; one feature-manifest scan now partitions those scenes into an exclusive serial batch while retaining parallel measurement and failure aggregation for the rest

Bath Day reaches the same demo URL, loading-progress, and BRDF LUT files already pinned for other applications; its immutable graph reuses those exact corpus paths and hashes instead of adding duplicate copies

after Draco joint values are repacked to glTF-valid unsigned shorts, the accessor writer still accepted signed int32 data even though no legal call site remained; its type now admits only float, unsigned-short, and unsigned-int buffers

optional DOM event registration initially risked a second browser-effect classifier; the erasure rule now reuses the statement lowerer's existing browser-local receiver and pure-argument predicates, while treating only the unreachable callback body specially

the default parallel parity sweep surfaced transient GPU child exits but discarded the otherwise healthy scenes after one attempt; the shared concurrent runner now drains the batch and retries only failed parity items once without overlap, while deterministic repeat failures remain fatal

LibreQuake's 2048-by-2048 RGBA light atlas was copied from PixelsTexture into every material TextureData record; SharedTextureBytes now retains one immutable backing allocation with copy-on-write mutation, removing repeated 16 MiB copies from startup

fixed numeric tuples were emitted as value-copying std::array objects even though JavaScript arrays preserve identity; Tuple now shares storage across ordinary copies and numeric spread explicitly clones it, keeping moving brush collision and visibility hull offsets synchronized with their entities

static numeric tables depended on the old innermost std::array representation; emitting Tuple only for the innermost numeric row preserves span-compatible table shape while retaining JavaScript identity for mutable tuples

the picking helper returned an optional std::array while compiler-generated numeric triples now use Tuple; the helper now returns the shared tuple abstraction consistently, avoiding a special conversion path

relative pointer lock used raw low-sensitivity motion and trusted SDL's implicit cursor behavior; it now requests system-scaled relative motion and explicitly hides and restores the cursor when capture changes

SharedTextureBytes and Tuple duplicated const-reference and rvalue construction and assignment implementations, and SharedTextureBytes exposed an unused vector accessor; by-value entry points and direct clone construction preserve behavior with less surface area

the Scene 21 shader-composition test depended on an ignored local capture and therefore skipped on every clean checkout while the registered Scene 21 MAD gate already checks the rendered behavior end to end; the ineffective test and its unused imports were removed
